query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In phosphorus‐containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, adding a minor amount of boron (as a dopant introduced into the molten alloy prior to quenching) will improve both the glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous structure relative to the identical base alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: A phosphorus‐containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy produced by conventional melt processing without the boron dopant, where the amorphous state is difficult to achieve or unstable.
generation.intervention: Introduce a controlled, minor addition of boron (e.g., a few atomic percent, precise value controlled by alloy design) into the phosphorus-containing alloy melt prior to quenching.
generation.conditions: Both the doped and undoped alloys are melted, homogenized, and quenched under identical conditions (same cooling rate, atmospheric settings, and processing route). The thermal stability and glass forming ability are then evaluated by standardized thermal analysis (e.g., differential scanning calorimetry, DSC) under controlled heating rates.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron atoms, when uniformly distributed at the atomic scale, are expected to disrupt short- and medium-range order, increasing atomic packing frustration and thereby impeding nucleation and crystal growth.
generation.mechanism: The boron dopant interferes with the atomic rearrangements necessary for crystallization by promoting chemical heterogeneity and configurational entropy. This disruption in atomic clustering enhances the glass-forming ability and raises the temperature at which crystallization sets in (i.e., increases the thermal stability of the amorphous phase).
generation.predicted_outcome: The primary measured properties are an improved glass-forming ability (evidenced by a lower critical cooling rate or higher probability of forming an amorphous phase) and an increased crystallization onset temperature (as measured by DSC) relative to the baseline alloy.
generation.baseline: The identical phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy processed without the minor boron addition.
generation.boundary: This effect is expected under identical melt processing and quenching conditions. The improvement is only predicted when the boron is uniformly incorporated and the processing route is consistent between the compared samples.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the improvement in glass-forming ability and the shift in crystallization temperature is uncertain without further empirical calibration; the hypothesis predicts a directional improvement rather than a precise quantitative change.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy with the conventional composition (control) and another set with a minor, controlled boron addition. Use identical melting, homogenization, and quenching procedures to form the amorphous state. Evaluate both sets using differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) to record the crystallization onset temperatures and determine the critical cooling rates required to avoid crystallization.
measurements: Critical cooling rate or glass formation probability
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-doped samples do not exhibit a statistically significant improvement in glass-forming ability (i.e., show no decrease in critical cooling rate or higher amorphous formation probability) and do not display an increased crystallization onset temperature compared to the control samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.
